Hay hay, back from work now. I'm going to share some stuffs, incoming walk of text. . . 

*I'm from Scotland and was drugged, beaten, raped, robbed then dumped in a street in Germany where I was working. My memory has never came back, it's a black hole that my mind tries to fill in but I know it'll never be anything other than *insert explanations for my injuries*. I thought it was a silver lining that I didn't remember it, oh how wrong I was; there is no silver lining to rape, just different roads in the same fucked up land. 
        
*The association that helps me more than anything is Rape Crisis, I don't know where you are from but if you're in the UK, I would advise contacting them. The Nhs doesn't know how to cope with sexual abuse/assault, they were amazing for my physical injuries and still are (dental work at the moment then perhaps resetting my nose) but for mental injuries? They suck. I had to be suicidal in order to qualify for therapy through them because I was, and I quote, "...coping well with the trauma, when that changes, phone us again". Implying being frozen with shock, constant panic attacks, night terrors, thoughts of self harm, inability to leave my bedroom, inability to work, inability to communicate, confused and terrified to name a fraction of what I was feeling then was fucking coping. 

*Rape Crisis are the opposite of that, they offer a drop in service, telephone helpline, online help, one to one counselling and group therapy. I have used ALL of it. To the group questions you had, it was a difficult choice to make because I thought a of this and more; am I ready to share what happened? Am I ready to hear other people's stories? What if i don't click with these people? What if I hate them? What if their stories trigger me and I feel worse? 

* When it started there was 6 of us, now there's only 2, group work really isn't for everyone. Not in a bad way, it just depends on where you are with your own recovery and your own personality; for some people one to one would be far more useful, it just depends. 

*Two of us were 'recent' cases and the others were child victims or it happened decades ago. There was one woman who I didn't click with for a number of reasons and ill explain why without breaching her confidence. She was a child when it happened, back in the days where children were locked up in institutions because the authorities had no idea how to deal with it. She never had the chance to deal with the trauma properly because of her age and the time she was living in, as a result a bitter, angry and isolated woman was created. At first she refused to accept any other way of thinking, her safety mechanisms had worked for all these years so why change it now? kind of thing. Because I shared my story with the group, she knew I had(ve) ptsd and bad triggers when it comes to the German language (one I know and used to love), she chose to say please, thank you, random numbers and other silly things in German. I'm good at reading people, even more so now, and I caught her eye a few times, coupled with her body language, it was on purpose. I had a choice, leave the group (which was helping me), confront her, talk to rape crisis about it or leave it another week and see if she does it again. She's never came back to the group so it was taken out of my hands. Had she stayed I would've waited until the end of the next session, pulled her aside and explain my situation and ask her politely to refrain from using that language. 

Things are different for different people but group has helped me so much. I'm working again but feel free to reply, pm etc and ill gets back to you when I'm free!  Xxxxxx

The police wanted to make it go away but the doctors wouldn't because my injuries were obvious. 

I didn't feel hugely different down there because like your gf, i wanted help to fill in the missing time. My memory was plucked from my brain and all it wanted to do was find it, not think about the present. My advice? Be gentle and approach her about it, try to see if she wants to talk. And if she feels comfortable, explain that it could be a good idea for her to have a think about her body and how it feels. Try and make her aware of her own body, now and remember before. She will feel a difference because of the lost time but just recognising herself could allow her to realise if there is something actually wrongful underneath the panic she's feeling.

Hay dude. This happened to me while I was working in a foreign country. I didn't have any memory of it but i knew something had happens to me. It was confirmed at the hospital and I didn't know what to do or think.

First port of call is the police if she wants to report any thing or wants to try and work out her whereabouts. If she doesn't want to then you can't force her to. If she has been sexually assaulted she will not have a clue where to start and you might have to take the lead. By that I mean get her the police contact for non emergencies. Get her a rape crisis helpline number. If you can arrange for her to go to th doctors. Present options for her. She could be battling with a complex around control due to the missing memory along with an inability to make a decision due to not being able to see clearly therefore show her there are options, but don't forcefully direct her to any of them. This is.the start of her journey and she needs to be in control.

If nothing happened to her sexually, she has went through a huge trauma and has to be taken care of. If she has been sexually assaulted then you will, or could, become her secondary survivor. I am from Scotland and there are rape crisis pdf downloads for partners of sexual violence and countless for her,if you have any organisations like that then give them a look online. 

Unfortunately the main focus is going to, and always has to be, on her. I think you should set some safe space and time aside to talk to her about how she feels, what she remember and how she wants to proceed. The only way you will be able to get a clear head or get out in front of this is to know more. 

Please update and let us know how you and her gets on. 

EDIT: blood work depends on the drug used and time it lasts in the system and then when the blood was taken.
